title: Neural pathways
prompt:
Create a 30-second silent English 1920×1080 educational animation about Neural pathways for Introduction to Neuroscience.
Use Remotion 4.0.410, React 19 and the introduction-to-neuroscience course kit. Reproduce the actual video in assets/source-kits/introduction-to-neuroscience/src/videos/ns06-neural-pathways.tsx; fps is 30.
Keep the same dark course palette and diagrams. Use the actual state transitions from the source, not a generic neural-network animation.

Scene plan:
1. 0–5s, route: The fingertip deforms slightly and a single signal packet appears at the peripheral input, while all central arrivals remain off. Why: A tactile input initiates activity in the sensory pathway. Visible result: The first signal exists at the right-hand input and has not appeared prematurely in cortex.
2. 5–12s, ascend: CircuitSignal moves along the right-side path through the spinal level to the medullary relay; relay arrival indicator remains off until the packet reaches its endpoint. Why: Upper-body discriminative touch ascends ipsilaterally before its first medullary relay. Visible result: The packet is visibly on the right side throughout this leg and ends at the medulla.
3. 12–18s, cross: The input packet terminates at the relay; an output packet follows a curved path across the midline into the left column. Relay identities stay fixed. Why: Second-order dorsal-column pathway neurons decussate in the medulla. Visible result: The packet crosses the dashed midline only at the medulla, and subsequently occupies the opposite side.
4. 18–25s, relay: The thalamic arrival event generates a final outgoing packet; it moves to left somatosensory cortex, whose arrival marker changes only at final contact. Why: The thalamus relays ascending touch information to cortex. Visible result: Thalamus is reached before cortex; the cortical response cannot precede the preceding relay.
5. 25–30s, sequence: Three numbered segment markers settle onto the existing route in arrival order, retaining the medullary crossing and final cortical endpoint. Why: A pathway is an ordered chain, not simultaneous activation of unrelated nodes. Visible result: The complete pathway, one crossing and terminal cortical arrival remain visible together.

All on-screen labels and narration-equivalent captions are concise English. Use no spoken audio or music. Preserve the specific objects, state bindings and timing above. Render the registered composition for this slug and inspect the final MP4 at the stored risk moments.
Reproduction requires the packaged TSX source, the course kit, Remotion/React dependencies, Chromium and ffmpeg. This prompt describes the reviewed artifact; it is not a self-contained promise of pixel-identical reproduction without those files.
final_title: Neural Pathways: A Touch Signal Crosses Sides
learning_objective: Trace a right-hand fine-touch signal through ascending relays and identify the medullary crossing.
core_conclusion: A neural pathway carries information through connected neurons; in the fine-touch example, the signal crosses in the medulla before reaching left cortex.

references.title: Neuroanatomy, Brainstem — Dorsal Column-Medial Lemniscus
references.supports: Fine-touch afferents ascend in dorsal columns, relay in medulla, cross, and relay through thalamus to postcentral cortex.

requirement_prompt:
Create a 15-second silent educational animation in Manim Community Edition.

Explain “Neural pathways” using this visual metaphor: “a glowing neural circuit carrying one signal for Neural pathways”. Dynamically demonstrate the core formula or conclusion: A neural pathway carries signals through a defined sequence of connected regions..

Use one continuous scene and one clear narrative line. Explain only this concept; do not add comparisons, extensions, or side cases. Structure the motion in three connected beats:
1. 0–3 seconds: establish the objects, input, or initial state.
2. 3–10.95 seconds: show at least two causally connected state changes that reveal the mechanism and progressively connect key variables or conclusions to the visual.
3. 10.95–12.45 seconds: resolve the result, invariant, or central insight.

Keep introducing meaningful animation information until 12.45 seconds. Hold the final still frame for no more than 2.55 seconds.

All on-screen titles, labels, and supporting annotations must be short English phrases in Arial. Use a bright, non-black background (#F7F3EA); main visual (#0B4F6C); secondary visual (#8B1E3F); highlight (#795500); and text (#172033). Maintain strong contrast and legibility.

Strict typography requirements:
- Render every complete title, label, phrase, or sentence as one native Text(...) object so every character shares one baseline.
- Never rebuild a line from separately positioned word or letter objects, and never align words by their individual bounding boxes.
- Create Arial text at a base font_size of 64, then uniformly scale the complete Text object to its final visual size; do not render explanatory text directly at a tiny font size.
- Preserve ordinary spaces inside the same Text object, set disable_ligatures=True, and do not add manual tracking, special-width spaces, or per-character offsets.

Use ThreeDScene for a genuinely spatial main visual: at least one core object must show volume, depth, or occlusion, and include one smooth camera move that reveals spatial structure. The 3D motion must clarify the concept rather than merely tilt a flat diagram. Render in 16:9.

Global rendering requirements:
- Never place plain English words, sentences, titles, or explanatory prose in MathTex, Tex, or inline LaTeX math mode. Use the native Text(...) component for all explanatory text and titles.
- If an English word is unavoidable inside a mathematical expression, explicitly wrap every word with \text{...}; never leave a word bare in algebra mode.
- Animate text at whole-word or whole-line granularity. Never split text into individually spaced letters or animate isolated letter spans.
- Do not use text-align: justify or the SVG textLength or lengthAdjust attributes.
- Use the final conclusion display as the video's opening poster frame; do not begin on an empty background.
